subject: Request: short-term forensic snapshot preservation & SIG/CAIQ evidence
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@caremesh.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: security+forensics@caremesh.com, mike@caremesh.com
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short-term preservation of debug snapshots for live incident (CareMesh)

Hi Naomi,

We spoke briefly on the phone this morning — thanks for taking this. CareMesh has an active investigation into a suspicious data pathway and we need Redwood's help to preserve a narrow set of debug snapshots and ephemeral traces so our incident responders can validate the timeline.

What we need from Redwood:
- A 45-day preservation hold on the ephemeral debug snapshots for tenant caremesh-prod (approx. 3.2GB compressed) starting now.
- An export packaged with checksums and chain-of-custody metadata (who exported, when, S3 path).
- SIG/CAIQ artifacts or a short attestation that confirm: how preserved snapshots are isolated, encryption at rest/in transit, and where audit logs will be retained for the preservation window.

Attachments: a short investigation summary with the IDs of the traces we want preserved (caremesh_investigation_summary.pdf).

Can Redwood confirm whether you can (a) place the limited hold without changing default account TTLs for other tenants, and (b) provide the small set of artifacts we can include with our regulator filing?

We are aiming to file an interim report with our regulator next week; a quick confirmation and an outline of the evidence package (preferably links we can include) will help.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Security Ops Lead, CareMesh Health
[attachment: caremesh_investigation_summary.pdf (PDF, 210KB)]

From: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
To: Elena Park <elena@caremesh.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term forensic snapshot preservation & SIG/CAIQ evidence

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the summary. Short answers up front: we can do a tenant-scoped hold for a narrowly scoped set of artifacts and we can produce an evidence bundle that covers the items you called out. A couple quick clarifying questions so we scope precisely:

1) Exact list of snapshot IDs / time ranges to preserve (I see the PDF but want explicit ids in a reply so our automation can pick them up).
2) Is the 45-day window measured from the time of export or from now? (we typically either: start hold now and allow export during the hold, or start from the export timestamp).
3) Do you need a signed attestation (legal) or a technical artifacts bundle (checksums + audit log links) only? If signed, I'll loop in Legal to provide the attestation form.

Action plan from our side after we get answers:
- Security (Jonas) will create an export job scoped to the IDs you confirm, store it in a customer-isolated encrypted bucket, compute SHA256 checksums, and record a preservation_manifest.csv with chain-of-custody fields.
- Infra will set a 45-day override TTL for those objects only — no change to tenant-level TTLs for other data.
- Compliance will produce the SIG/CAIQ-checklist snippets relevant to preservation and a brief attestation describing the controls and audit retention.

I cc'd Jonas (security), Marissa (legal) and Priya (compliance) to confirm feasibility and expected timelines. If you can reply with the exact IDs and whether you need a signature, we'll target delivery within 48 hours.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Customer Security Partner 
Redwood Inference

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, Elena Park <elena@caremesh.com>
Cc: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term forensic snapshot preservation & SIG/CAIQ evidence

Elena / Naomi — technical update and proposed preservation manifest.

We can execute the requested flow. Notes:
- Scope: we will preserve snapshot ids: cs-2026-11-01-az1, cs-2026-10-29-batch-7, cs-2026-11-01-ephem-42 (please confirm if any missing).
- Hold timing: Redwood recommends starting the hold immediately (so ephemeral cleanup is inhibited) and exporting within the next 24 hours; the 45-day countdown will be measured from the export timestamp by default (so you get a full 45-day window after we package). If you want the clock to start now, state that explicitly.
- Storage and custody: export will be written to an encrypted S3 bucket in our us-west-2 region under path: s3://redwood-preserve/caremesh/20261103-<jobid>/ with bucket-level ACLs restricted to the preservation-run UUID, Security, and your read-only link. Objects will be AES-256 encrypted with a CMK (customer-isolation flag). We'll provide SHA256 checksums and a preservation_manifest.csv which will include: filename, object_size, sha256, exported_by (redwood service account), export_timestamp, export_job_id.
- Audit trail: a dedicated audit feed will be created and retained for 180 days for the preservation job, including who accessed the manifest and export. That feed is independent of tenant TTLs.
- Access: we can create a time-limited, read-only pre-signed URL (or provide a temporary IAM role if CareMesh wants direct access).

Attached is a sample manifest template and a short internal checklist we'll use to keep chain-of-custody. After Elena confirms the exact IDs and whether the 45 days should start now or at export, we'll kick the job and post the manifest and links.

-Jonas
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

[attachment: preservation_manifest.csv (CSV, 1KB)]

On Mon, Nov 2, 2026 at 8:03 AM naomi.feldman@redwood.ai wrote:

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term forensic snapshot preservation & SIG/CAIQ evidence

Elena — legal here. Confirming Redwood can issue a short attestation describing the preservation activity and the controls in place (isolation, encryption, audit logging, and custody chain). We will not change account-wide TTLs.

Next steps for a signed attestation:
- I'll prepare a one-page attestation doc that covers the preservation window and the exported artifact handling.
- Please confirm the caremesh contact for signature routing and whether you prefer DocuSign or an emailed PDF.

If you only need technical artifacts (manifest + checksums + audit links), we can deliver those immediately after the export. If you need the legal attestation, allow 24 business hours for review and signature.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
